newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African mine says its workers died in clashes.
newsitem.headline: S.African mine says its workers died in clashes.

text.p: South African mineowners Impala Platinum Holdings confirmed on Tuesday that most of the 32 people killed in ethnic clashes at the weekend were their workers.
"Of the people identified thus far...the majority were Impala employees," the company said in a statement. "Investigation by police into the deaths is intense, but as yet no arrests have been made."

Police said fighting broke out at a squatter camp called Freedom Park near Impala's Wildebeesfontein mine in Rustenburg northwest of Johannesburg on Saturday after a Xhosa shopowner killed a Sotho man for allegedly stealing milk from his shop.
Police and soldiers were brought in to keep the feuding tribal groups apart. On Tuesday, police were still patrolling the area but no further violence was anticipated.

Impala spokesman Humphrey Oliphant acknowledged 67 percent of people living in the squatter camp were employed by the mine but said this had "unfortunately" resulted from the company's attempts to dismantle its hostel system.

"Only 40 percent of our employees now reside in a hostel," he said, adding the mine was developing serviced sites in an effort to address the squatting issue. At its three remaining hostels, workers were not grouped on an ethnic basis, he said.
South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers', the largest in the industry, has condemned the continuing ethnic feuds on mines and has vowed to help identify the culprits.
The industry is built on a labour system under which men leave their wives and families for months at a time to work on the mines. Hostels are largely segregated on ethnic lines.
